text: A real compliance requirement is almost always one specific question: who accessed this data, when, and were they authorized to at that time — an actual query someone can run and get a real answer to.

Audit logs tell you who touched a table, not whether they should have. Lineage tells you what's exposed, not who actually queried it. Access control state tells you what a user was entitled to see, not whether they ran a query. None answers the real question alone.

Take a real question: did anyone outside the approved group ever see an unmasked SSN in Q3. Answering it means checking the audit log, each user's group membership at that timestamp, and the masking policy actually active on that column at that same moment.

GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2 each specify retention periods and response obligations, but none invent a new technical mechanism. They all rest on the same backbone: can you actually answer who accessed what, when, and was it authorized.

Chapter 6 is complete: row and column security at scale, Delta Sharing, secrets, and now a real compliance answer built from all of it. Next up, Chapter 7, the course's final chapter — DP-750 exam prep and the capstone.
